subject.title: Windows Tray/Hub: missing deviceFamily causes metadata-upgrade loop on restart

question: Should this issue stay open here as the OpenClaw release-facing tracker while the source fix is made in `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node`, or should it be transferred/duplicated there first?
rationale: The bug affects a shipped OpenClaw release asset, but the implicated source code is in the Windows companion repository and the final user fix requires signed installer promotion back through this repository.

options.title: Route to Windows repo and keep this open
options.body: Track the user-facing OpenClaw release issue here while opening or linking a Windows companion source fix and closing only after a signed promoted build is available.

options.title: Transfer to Windows repo
options.body: Move the source-level issue to `openclaw/openclaw-windows-node` and leave this repository with only release-promotion follow-up if needed.

options.title: Add gateway compatibility workaround
options.body: Patch the core gateway to tolerate the Windows operator omission, but this weakens the cleaner metadata-pinning boundary and is not the preferred fix.

recommendation.title: Route to Windows repo and keep this open
recommendation.body: Track the user-facing OpenClaw release issue here while opening or linking a Windows companion source fix and closing only after a signed promoted build is available.

likelyOwner.reason: The evidence points to the Windows companion operator client as the source fix, and shanselman is the strongest available Windows companion routing owner.
